bbox_coordinate_contract.units: integer coordinates in [0,1000), x normalized by input width and y by input height
bbox_coordinate_contract.rotation_frame: Coordinates are relative to the exact image supplied to the model. Harness applies EXIF transpose then composites alpha onto white before inference; fixture rotations are baked into the supplied raster, so compare to ground-truth boxes transformed into that same raster. No inverse transform to an earlier unrotated source is applied.

prompt.text:
Analyze the document structure and extract text content. Return a single JSON array in natural reading order. Each element follows this schema: `{"bbox": [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max], "category": "string", "content": "string"}` Rules: 1. The bbox coordinates are integers scaled to [0, 1000). 2. The category is exactly one of: ["abstract", "algorithm", "aside_text", "chart", "content", "display_formula", "doc_title", "figure_title", "footer", "footer_image", "footnote", "formula_number", "header", "header_image", "image", "inline_formula", "number", "paragraph_title", "reference_content", "seal", "table", "text", "vertical_text", "vision_footnote"]. 3. The content formatting depends on category: - For "footer_image", "header_image", "image", or "chart": write as an HTML image tag . - For "display_formula" or "inline_formula": write in LaTeX. - For "table": write as a standard HTML `...
`. - Otherwise: write in Markdown. 4. Output must be strictly valid JSON. Properly escape quotes and special characters inside content.
